summary: The bottom shortcut strip no longer includes deletion hints. Delete commands and their shortcuts remain available.
To panel uses an underlined P. Go to file has no Enter suffix and uses the primary button style while results have focus; Search is primary in query fields.
Name columns shrink to available space. Narrow panels hide Modified, then Size, then Type, restoring them as space returns without losing column preferences, cursor or marks.
Sort headers accept clicks across their full area while keeping resize handles usable.
Panels and controls have square corners. Selection in the inactive panel uses a faint background.
A command menu replaces the large title inside the window.
F12 and a Feedback button select elements in every application dialog without losing its draft or selection.
History, Frequent locations and Favorites share one navigation window with Left/Right list selection. Frequent locations use qualified active visits and a three-day score half-life.
Panels automatically monitor their directories and preserve cursor, selection and scroll when external files change.
Type, size and modified values are vertically centered with the file name.
File rows display Windows shell icons for folders and file types. Native handles are released and icon loading stays off the UI thread.
The final column fills remaining space without a trailing resize handle. View > Reset column widths restores defaults with room for ten-gigabyte byte counts.
History is a subtle text link without a dropdown arrow. Hover help shows Alt+Down.
Entering a child directory selects its parent entry so a second Enter returns. History and session restore still preserve saved cursors.
Alt name jumping handles physical key events without relying on text input, avoids duplicate text events, and tries the loaded Windows keyboard layouts.
All application windows were rendered and reviewed. Panel headers, footers, history rows and dialog margins are compact; small forms fit their content and action buttons align to the right.
Start name search with Alt and a letter, then release Alt and keep typing. Unmatched letters are ignored. Navigation, pointer movement, commands, Escape and focus changes clear the prefix.
Only the active history column has a selection. Switching columns remembers each cursor. Compact single-line paths fit more locations, and the dialog height adapts to its contents.
The Type heading and file type values share the same horizontal center. Size headings align with byte counts, and cell padding matches the header layout.
Ctrl+C copies the whole command when no text is selected, keeping the draft, caret and selection. Selected text still copies normally.
The command directory trims from the left and can use 510 pixels. Narrow windows reserve space for command input. Hover help shows the full path.
Sort headings use larger, light text centered vertically against a dark blue background.
Windows launch errors show the target and a short reason without repeating the working directory or process details.
Keyboard shortcuts have visible separators and wrap to keep every command visible in narrow windows.
The operation strip appears only after one second of running work and hides after completion. Operation history remains available from View > File operations.
Deletion uses a short question and a Yes button with initial focus. Enter confirms the selected deletion mode.
F5 and F6 confirm an editable destination. Shift+F5 copies in the active panel. Delete and Shift+Delete default to Recycle Bin and permanent deletion; both modes can be selected in the confirmation.
The operation summary has a fixed height. Long paths use an ellipsis and remain available in hover help.
The conflict dialog uses a compact two-column comparison, short action labels, and full paths in hover help.
Escape clears the command line and returns focus to the active file panel without moving its cursor.
The shortcut strip omits Tab, Enter, Escape and plain arrow navigation. Less obvious shortcuts remain visible.
Copy and Move appear in the confirmation body with the selected name or item count and the destination.
Existing regular files are skipped without a question only when contents, size, modification time and basic attributes match.
Copy completion preserves the source cursor, marks and scroll position. Copying onto source paths is rejected before submission; batches never create automatic duplicates.

Operations count files before changing them, show processed files against that total, and display a byte progress bar with an estimated remaining time. Selected roots and file totals have separate labels.
Shift+Up and Shift+Down toggle the departed row and move the cursor. Plain arrows preserve marks so keyboard users can skip rows and copy only marked files.
Deletion modes use underlined R and P access keys. The highlighted Yes button confirms the selected mode on Enter, including while a mode has focus.
Marked files have an amber check and file name, separate from the cursor. Shift+Up and Shift+Down toggle the departed row, so repeating the action removes its mark.
Escape clears file marks and keeps the cursor. Escape from the command line also clears marks and returns focus to files. Editors and search keep their own first Escape action.
Table rows stay inside their viewport. Scroll bars reserve their own space, and an opaque footer has a clear top boundary.
Recycle Bin and Permanently show underlined R and P access keys instead of shortcut text in parentheses. Alt+R and Alt+P select the modes.

The Yes label has no Enter hint. Default actions share a blue style and respond to Enter in folder, transfer, delete, conflict and navigation dialogs. Multiline comments keep Enter for a new line and Ctrl+Enter to submit.
Cursor and mark changes keep the same row size and column positions. Fitting columns do not gain a horizontal scroll bar; wider columns still scroll.
The cursor always uses the same blue background, with a faint background in the inactive panel. Marked files always use an amber name and check, including when the cursor is on a marked file.
Up, Down, Home, End, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End, Page Up, Page Down and name jumping move the cursor without clearing file marks. Escape clears marks.
The cursor uses a background without a layout border. Moving the cursor keeps text, icons and cells at the same positions.

Shift+Home, Shift+End, Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page Down fill an incomplete range and remove a fully marked range when repeated. Marks outside the range remain unchanged, and the parent entry is excluded.

The navigation window no longer shows the obvious-keyboard hint. Static text has a shared feedback hit-test surface, visual hit testing includes disabled actions, and feedback identifies the nearest meaningful element before its outer window. The architecture documents the rule and pointer checks cover the application dialogs.
Unavailable image modes stay disabled. Image decoding finishes before a mode change; unsupported, oversized or damaged images keep a working text or hex view.
The read-only content has no accent outline when focused or hovered.
Reading percentage is shown at the right of the combined title and menu row, above the scroll bar. The status line keeps mode, encoding, wrapping and byte counts.
The viewer combines its menu, file name, percentage and window controls in one title row. The window keeps a resize border and a title-bar drag region.

Viewers are independent, non-modal windows. File panels remain available, multiple viewers keep separate files, and closing one viewer preserves the others. Automatic updates wait until all viewers close.

In feedback mode a double-click sends one normal click to the selected control and keeps selection active. Menus can be opened before selecting a child item. Comments, saved sessions and the refinement list retain the click path.
File icons keep their native Windows pixels without resampling. The selected source is large enough for the display scale, including after a scale change. Panel text uses a larger font.
The viewer remembers the last query across files and viewer windows. F3 reuses it, and Find selects the previous query so typing replaces it.
Ctrl+Backslash opens the active panel's current drive root without changing the opposite panel.
Ctrl+Backquote opens the home directory. The shortcut uses the same physical key for English Backquote and Russian yo.
The refinement list opens on a separate Open tab. Resolved comments have their own tab, counts and selection. Newer comments appear first within each tab.

Up and Down switch query fields. Alt+F selects File name and Alt+T selects Containing text. Alt+Down opens each field's saved query history. The wildcard option says Treat * and ? as text and explains that it does not require whole words.

Search results use compact single-line rows with larger path text and a separate preview column. Plain text search streams long lines without a line-length failure. Coverage issues have a short summary and collapsed details.

Editing query fields or options keeps the current results and workers. A pending-settings message explains how to apply the draft. Starting the changed query cancels and joins the old workers before replacing them.
Search does not restart an unchanged query while it is running. Changed settings are applied only when the user starts the next search.
Enter starts search from query fields and checkboxes. It does not toggle a checkbox. Space remains the checkbox toggle key.
The matching excerpt has its own right-hand Preview column. Paths and line numbers stay in compact aligned rows.

Skipped scope separates known Git-ignored files, Git-ignored folder roots and standard folders. Expand details to inspect paths, reasons and exact Git rules. The expansion button appears only when locations were skipped and names the relevant scope. Folder contents are not counted.
Search results use a native table with resizable Path, Line and Preview columns. Column widths are saved with the workspace and restored when search opens again.

Skipped locations use compact single-line rows with Path and Reason columns, readable text and resizable saved widths. Git rules appear in Reason; the repeated folder and counting notes are removed from rows.
Whole name matches the complete name instead of a substring. Wildcard masks still match the complete name. The mode is saved with search settings.
The redundant line explaining name matching, archives and binary files is removed. Context help stays in control tooltips.
The extra feedback row above Search in is removed. Feedback is available in the bottom action row and through F12.
The status uses Complete, matches, checked and skipped. The same skipped term appears in the details and the Search skipped files action; selected scope and deferred are removed from this flow.

Search is an independent non-modal window without an owner that keeps it above the main window. Panel commands and dialogs remain available. Alt+F7 restores the same search window and keeps its results; automatic updates still wait until search closes.

Alt name jumping matches text anywhere in a file or directory name. The leftmost occurrence wins, so prefix matches have priority. Equal positions use the first visible row. Layout translation and ignored unmatched input still work.
Alt name search highlights the matching text in every matching name. Up and Down cycle through matching rows without clearing the query. Escape, Tab and other commands clear the query and highlights.
Starting search focuses the result table. Up from the first result returns to Containing text; Down from Containing text returns to results. Other result arrows keep normal row navigation.
Skipped locations have separate Reason, Path and Rule / source columns. Reason uses a short label; the source column includes the exact ignore-file path, line and rule.
Search issues use a compact table with Reason, Path and Explanation columns. Archive, access, Git and other issues have short reason labels and separate explanations.
Double-click a skipped path or issue row to run the same query at that location in the existing search window. Folder, single-file and nested-archive roots are supported.
Contains and Whole name are choices in a compact dropdown beside File name. The name-matching mode is no longer a checkbox in the general options row.
Search and Stop appear below both query fields and the options. Their placement shows that Search applies to the complete query.

File and folder icons keep a fixed 16-DIP layout size when the window changes DPI. Windows icons are rendered to the exact physical size for the current display scale, so 32-pixel shell icons no longer enlarge rows on 125% or 150% monitors. Both panels are checked through repeated 100%, 125%, 150%, 200% and return transitions.
